title: Neura Robotics launches multimodal AI model that gives robots perception and memory
key_facts: Neura Robotics launched Neuron AI, a multimodal foundation model for physical AI.
It combines 3D vision, touch, audio, robot state and language, plus a memory function so robots can keep track of objects out of view.
It is trained on real-world robot data, simulated data and human demonstrations from people wearing sensor suits, across five Neura robot types.
Neura says it was developed and trained in-house in Metzingen, Germany.
Neura will demonstrate its 4NE1 humanoid doing an eleven-minute laundry sequence with the model at Nvidia GTC Berlin from 20 to 22 Oct.
David Reger, founder and CEO of Neura, is quoted on the launch.
quote_evidence: Neura Robotics has launched Neuron AI, its multimodal foundation model for physical AI.
In addition, Neuron AI has a memory function.

At Nvidia GTC Berlin 2026, Neura will demonstrate its humanoid robot 4NE1 (which means “For Anyone” phonetically) performing an eleven-minute laundry-handling sequence with the current version of Neuron AI.
why_it_matters_hint: Robots that combine touch, sound and memory could handle tasks cameras alone cannot, but this is a company launch without outside tests.
notes: Reads as a company press release; no independent results.
